statusText: Tail remains in the low band; stress is elevated by technology weakness, event risk and geopolitical headlines, while persistent one-way NQ structure is not verified.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Current evidence does not establish persistent mean-reversion failure.
headline: Low Tail risk with elevated technology and event stress
body: Monday's Nasdaq decline was led by technology and semiconductor weakness while Treasury yields and oil eased. The setup raises Stress, but available overnight evidence does not verify a persistent NQ no-retracement path. The main near-term conditional danger window is the U.S. data and cash-open sequence.

lookbackSummary: The exact 00:00 UTC slot uses the previously published ChatGPT assessment; no qualifying published assessment was resolved for the other preceding clock-hour slots, so those remain unavailable rather than reconstructed.
outlookSummary: Tail is expected to remain low overnight, move into WATCH only around the U.S. data and cash-open sequence, then recede if price discovery becomes two-way. Stress remains higher because rates, geopolitics, technology weakness and major Wednesday catalysts can produce volatility without a persistent no-retracement path.

forecast.analysis: Current evidence remains mixed after Monday's tech-led Nasdaq decline. Stress is elevated, but available overnight evidence does not verify persistent one-way NQ structure or failed mean reversion.
drivers: Overnight NQ path evidence remains incomplete

news.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq end down on tech stocks, investors weigh Iran moves

forecast.analysis: Thin overnight liquidity can exaggerate moves; Tail stays low unless futures begin holding an extreme with shallow or failed retracements.
Asia-to-Europe handoff is a structure checkpoint. Sustained directional alignment across tech, yields and breadth would be needed to move Tail out of the low band.
European liquidity should improve evidence quality. Orderly two-way trade would support low Tail; repeated extension after weak retracements would challenge it.
European cash participation can clarify semiconductor and megacap leadership. Conflicting cross-asset signals would favor a mixed regime.
Rates remain a background stressor, while lower Monday yields conflict with the tech selloff. Tail depends on whether futures convert that tension into directional efficiency.
drivers: Monday yield decline versus tech weakness

forecast.analysis: With U.S. catalysts still ahead, anticipation can lift volatility without proving mean-reversion failure. Persistent extension remains the key Tail checkpoint.
Premarket positioning becomes more reactive to headlines. Conditional alignment of semiconductors, megacaps and yields would increase directional risk.
Approaching U.S. morning data, Stress rises while Tail remains below the block threshold absent observed one-way price structure.
U.S. premarket liquidity improves and event sensitivity rises. A failed retracement sequence would matter more for Tail than the scheduled releases themselves.
Consumer-confidence and housing data approach. Event uncertainty raises Stress; Tail only rises materially if the resulting price path becomes persistently directional.
drivers: Stress before release, not automatic Tail

forecast.analysis: The 14:00 UTC data cluster is a defined whipsaw checkpoint. Tail moves into WATCH conditionally because release-driven repricing can overlap with the cash-open approach.
After the data, the key test is whether NQ retraces meaningfully or extends repeatedly. Orderly two-way discovery would pull Tail back toward the low band.
The U.S. cash open is the highest near-term path-risk window. Opening-auction continuation with shallow pullbacks would be stronger Tail evidence than the data surprise alone.
Once the opening auction matures, Tail should recede if breadth and tech leadership stop aligning directionally and retracements normalize.
Mid-morning conditions remain sensitive to technology leadership. Persistent session-extreme holding would keep WATCH risk alive; two-way trade would normalize it.
Late morning typically offers better evidence on whether the open created a durable trend. Tail stays low in the base case without repeated failed retracements.
Early afternoon has fewer scheduled catalysts. Stress remains moderate-to-elevated from rates, geopolitics and AI positioning, but Tail is conditional on path persistence.
Afternoon liquidity can expose whether morning direction is durable. A balanced tape would support normal/mixed conditions rather than a Tail escalation.
Into the final two cash hours, trend persistence matters more than headlines. Tail rises only if NQ is conditionally holding an extreme with weak counter-moves.
Power-hour risk is modestly higher because an established directional day can accelerate. Without that setup, the expected state remains low Tail.
The cash close can amplify flows, but a closing move alone is not pathological. Repeated extension without retracement would be required for a stronger Tail state.
Post-close liquidity thins while attention shifts toward Wednesday's major macro and Nvidia catalysts. Those future events raise Stress, not current Tail by themselves.
Overnight positioning ahead of Wednesday's GDP/PCE and Nvidia results can remain cautious. Tail stays low unless fresh futures structure becomes persistently one-way.
